========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, doctor, it's... it's a bit hard to explain, but I suppose what really made me finally pick up the phone and come in today is that my eating has just gotten all turned around lately. I used to be so good about my schedule, you know, having my little meals at the proper times, setting the table for myself even if it's just me. But now, it's like my whole internal clock is broken. Some days I'll just be sitting in the living room, maybe looking out the window, and I'll glance over at the clock and it's suddenly past three or four in the afternoon, and I realize I completely forgot lunch. Just entirely slipped my mind, which isn't like me at all. 

And then, on the flip side of that, there are other days where I just can't seem to settle down. I'll wander into the kitchen and just stand right there at the counter—not even pulling out a chair to sit down properly—and I'll just start eating whatever is in front of me. Mostly crackers, or whatever sweets I have tucked away in the cupboards. I'll just stand there eating and eating. And the strangest part of it all is that nothing even tastes right anymore. I'll be chewing on a cookie or a cracker, and it's just... dull. Like chewing on cardboard. There's no real flavor to it, no joy in it at all, but I just keep standing there putting it in my mouth anyway. It's just all so out of sorts, and it's been bothering me so much because I just don't understand why my appetite is doing this...

Well, yes, actually, now that you mention it... there is something that's been just going round and round in my mind, and I know it sounds odd, I really do. It's exhausting, really, because I can't stop thinking about it, even when I'm trying to watch my evening programs or make a cup of tea. I just keep wondering, what is the message? Well, doctor, that's just the thing, isn't it? My daughter, when I finally did hint at it the other day while we were having our Sunday tea—she brought over those lovely lemon scones from the bakery down on Main Street—she said, "Oh, Mom, your eyes are just playing tricks on you, you need new reading glasses." You feel it right down in your bones. It's real. \n\nAnd it's not just random mistakes, either. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, like I was saying just a moment ago... I know it sounds so very odd to say it out loud again, but yes, absolutely. I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or purposely hidden from me by someone who is pulling the strings behind the scenes. It really does feel like the hospital administration, or maybe even someone in my own family who is working with them, is controlling the whole thing. 

I've thought long and hard about how they're managing it, sitting there in the evenings. You see, we’ve always kept a spare key under the heavy ceramic frog on the back porch—my late husband Arthur bought that frog at a garden center over in Shelbyville back in, oh, it must have been 1998, or maybe '99—and I think they found it and are using it. They must wait until I go out to the grocery store on Tuesday mornings. I always go on Tuesdays, you see, because that's when they mark down the canned goods and the bakery items, and I like to get there right when the doors open. And while I'm out, they just slip right in through the back door. 

They must be coordinating the whole thing just to send me these little messages through the records. Why else would someone go through all the trouble of sneaking into a 74-year-old woman's spare bedroom just to alter the middle initial on an old hospital discharge paper or hide a billing statement from 2004? It has to be them orchestrating it. I just... I can't quite figure out how they know exactly when I'm leaving the house, unless they're parked down the street watching my driveway. I mean, it's a quiet neighborhood, you'd think Mrs. Gable next door would notice a strange car or someone walking up my path, but she's half deaf and never leaves her sunroom anyway, bless her heart, so she's no help at all. So yes, doctor, someone is definitely controlling it. They are going out of their way to manipulate those papers and leave me these messages in the folders, I just know it.

I’d open the curtains, let the sun in, maybe listen to the birds for a bit while I put the kettle on. But now, it’s just this gray, heavy blanket over everything. I just lie there thinking, 'What’s the point of getting up?' And it’s not just a passing feeling, it lingers. I’ll finally get myself out of bed, but that heavy feeling just follows me around the house all day, from the bedroom to the kitchen to the living room. It’s exhausting, really, just feeling so... weighed down by it all. I keep hoping I’ll wake up and feel like my old self again, but it’s just been this same dreary feeling morning after morning.\n\nDoctor: Have you been having any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, actually, now that you mention it... there is something that's been just going round and round in my mind, and I know it sounds odd, I really do. I've even hesitated to mention it to my daughter because she might think I'm just getting confused in my old age, but I'm not. You see, I have this old wooden filing cabinet in the spare bedroom—my late husband bought it at an estate sale back in 1982, beautiful oak thing—and that's where I keep all our important papers. Birth certificates, old hospital records, the deed to the house, all neatly organized in manila folders. \n\nBut lately, when I go in there to check on things, I get this overwhelming feeling... no, I *know*... that certain dates and names in those family papers are being changed. Or hidden from me. I'll look at a hospital bill from years ago, and the dates just don't line up with what I remember, or a middle initial on a document will look slightly altered. It's like... like the hospital, or maybe even someone in the family, is slipping in there when I'm not looking and rearranging things. And it's not just to mess with my files, no, it feels like they are sending me little messages through the records. Like there's a code or a secret meaning in why that specific date was changed, or why that particular paper was moved to the back of the folder. I'll sit on the edge of the guest bed for hours, just staring at these papers, trying to decipher what they're trying to tell me. It's exhausting, really, because I can't stop thinking about it, even when I'm trying to watch my evening programs or make a cup of tea. I just keep wondering, what is the message? Why are they doing this to my papers?\n\nDoctor: Do you believe these changes to your papers are actually happening, or do you think it might be a mistake or your imagination?\n\nPatient: Well, doctor, that's just the thing, isn't it? My daughter, when I finally did hint at it the other day while we were having our Sunday tea—she brought over those lovely lemon scones from the bakery down on Main Street—she said, \"Oh, Mom, your eyes are just playing tricks on you, you need new reading glasses.\" But I know it's not my eyes. I've had the same prescription for three years, Dr. Henderson checked them himself just last November. No, it's not a mistake, and it's certainly not my imagination. \n\nI know it sounds odd to someone on the outside, I really do. If someone told me this ten years ago, I might have thought they were a bit touched. But when you're sitting there, holding a piece of paper you've looked at a dozen times over the last thirty years, and suddenly the date of my husband's knee surgery is off by two days, or the spelling of a doctor's name has an extra 'e' at the end... you just know. You feel it right down in your bones. It's real. \n\nAnd it's not just random mistakes, either. Why else would they change the date on the deed to the house, just slightly? It has to mean something. It’s a message, I’m sure of it. I just haven’t quite pieced together what it is they’re trying to tell me yet, but I know it's happening. It really does feel like the hospital administration, or maybe even someone in my own family who is working with them, is controlling the whole thing. \n\nI've thought long and hard about how they're managing it, sitting there in the evenings. It really, truly is. \n\nBecause, like I keep saying—and I know I keep coming back to this, and I know it sounds odd to keep repeating it, but it's just so heavy on my mind—I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. Well, it certainly doesn't feel good. It makes my chest tight and my stomach all fluttery. I'll be sitting there in the evening, the television is on—I usually watch Wheel of Fortune, Pat Sajak is just so comforting, though I know he's retiring soon, which is a shame—and I can't even focus on the word puzzles. I can't even enjoy my evening because I'm just thinking about those folders in the oak cabinet. I'm sitting there thinking, what does the altered date mean? Why did they hide Arthur's billing statement? \n\nIf they aren't trying to harm me, then why on earth are they being so incredibly secretive about it all? Why not just call me on the telephone? I have a perfectly good landline. It's one of those old cream-colored ones hanging on the kitchen wall, with the long cord. Well, yes, of course they are. I mean... whose else would they be about? I know I must sound like a broken record today, and I know it sounds odd to keep bringing it up, but I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. It feels like they are trying to tell me something specific about my past, or maybe something I missed, or something I’m supposed to do now that I'm on my own. I’ll sit there in the armchair with my cup of decaf Earl Grey tea—I simply can't drink regular tea after three o'clock or I'll be up all night staring at the ceiling fan, my system just can't handle the caffeine anymore—and I just look at these altered documents, trying to decipher what my role in all this puzzle is. Because it has to be about me, doctor. It’s my life they’re editing. I just haven't figured out exactly what the message about my life is supposed to mean yet, but they wouldn't go through all this trouble if it weren't specifically meant for my eyes.

How long? Well, let me sit and think on that for just a moment... 

Because it certainly hasn't been forever. Arthur and I, we always kept everything so meticulously organized, and I never had a single reason to second-guess a piece of mail or a medical record. I remember just standing there with the folder in my hands, completely forgetting about the melting meat in the garage, just staring at this message someone had left for me in the margins of Arthur's old hospital bill. 

So it's been thirteen months of this. A year and a month of just... trying to figure out what these messages are supposed to mean, day in and day out. It feels like so much longer, to be perfectly honest with you, because when you spend every single evening worrying about your own files being edited behind your back, time just drags on so slowly. Mistaken? Well... I suppose anyone can be mistaken about anything, can't they? I mean, I’m not so stubborn that I can’t admit when I’ve made a simple error. Just last week, for instance, I was absolutely certain I had bought a tin of evaporated milk for my tea—I always use evaporated milk, never fresh, because it lasts so much longer in the cupboard and Arthur got me into the habit of it decades ago—but when I checked the pantry shelf, it just wasn't there. So I know I can be wrong about everyday things. 

And I know... well, I know it sounds odd. I really do know how it sounds when I say it out loud to you in a doctor's office. I'm not a foolish woman. But when it comes to these papers... I just can't shake it. I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me on purpose. It's not just a typo here or a smudge there, which is what I tried to tell myself at first. 

I’ll sit there with my reading glasses on—the ones with the little rhinestones on the corners that Susan bought me for my seventieth birthday, because she said I needed something a little more stylish—and I’ll stare at a date on a discharge summary, and I’ll tell myself, 'Now, you’re just misinterpreting this, it's just a clerical error.' But then I see the name next to it, and the middle initial is suddenly missing, or a letter is swapped, and that feeling just washes right back over me. It feels so deliberate, like the hospital, or maybe even someone in the family, is sending me little messages through the records. 

It’s like they know I’m the only one who keeps these old files, the only one who takes the time to look through them, so they’re hiding these things right there in plain sight for me to find. So, even though I try my hardest to tell myself I might just be mistaken, the feeling that they are changing these things to communicate with me... it's just too strong to ignore. I keep going back to it. I just wish I knew exactly what the hospital or whoever it is actually wants me to do with the information, because it's terribly exhausting trying to piece it all together on my own.

Control? Oh, heavens no, doctor. None at all. And that is perhaps the most distressing part of this whole ordeal. If I had any control over it, I would have put a stop to it months ago, I assure you. 

I've actually tried to stop it, you know. But it didn't make a lick of difference. When I opened the box three days later to check a billing statement... well, there it was again. The ink had shifted.

It's exactly like the hospital, or perhaps someone in our own family, is determined to send me these little messages through the records, and they somehow find a way to alter the pages even when they are locked tight in a metal box. 

So no, I don't have any control over it whatsoever. It just happens, right under my nose, despite my best efforts to keep everything secure. I'm just left sitting there at my dining room table, trying to decipher what on earth they're trying to tell me this time. It’s exhausting, doctor, it truly is, having to constantly be on guard when you don't even have the power to stop it from happening.

Well, Doctor, I feel a bit like we're beating a dead horse, as my father used to say. Like I was just saying a few minutes ago, I know it sounds odd—I really am fully aware of how strange it must sound to a professional like yourself, and I don't blame you for asking again to make sure you understood me correctly. But I do still believe it, because it simply hasn't stopped. I still keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me on purpose. \n\nJust this morning, for instance, right before I put my good wool coat on to come down here to see you—the navy blue one, because there was quite a chill in the air today and my joints ache if I don't bundle up—I took one last look at a stack of Medicare summaries I had left out on the credenza in the hallway. I wasn't even going to look at them, I was just looking for my house keys, but my eye caught the top page. And sure enough, a middle initial that was clear as day on Tuesday was just... gone. Obscured. Hidden completely. \n\nSo yes, even though I try to rationalize it and tell myself I'm just an old woman with too much time on her hands, I still feel exactly like the hospital, or perhaps someone in the family who knows I check these things, is sending me little messages through the records. It’s an ongoing thing, doctor, it didn't just happen once and go away. The papers keep changing. I just wish they would come out and tell me what they want to say plainly, instead of all this hiding and shifting of the ink, because it takes up so much of my day just trying to keep track of it all.\n\nDoctor: Do you still think the changes in your papers are real, even if no one else can see them?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, doctor. I know we keep going over this, and I know I’ve said it a few times already today, but yes, I absolutely do believe they are real. \n\nI actually tried showing my daughter, Susan, just last Sunday. She came over for a roast—I always do a small beef roast on Sundays, even if it’s just the two of us now, with carrots and those little red potatoes she’s liked since she was a little girl in pigtails—and after dinner, I brought out one of the folders. I pointed right to a discharge paper from 2018, right where the ink was different, where the name was clearly altered. And she just sighed, you know how daughters sigh, that heavy sort of exhale, and told me it looked perfectly normal to her. She said it was just a smudge from the hospital's printer and that I was working myself up over nothing. \n\nBut I know what I see, doctor. I know it sounds terribly odd to keep harping on it, and I know Susan thinks I'm just being a fussy old woman, but I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. It’s not a printer smudge. It’s just too specific. Even if Susan can't see it, or perhaps just doesn't *want* to see it because it makes her uncomfortable, I know the hospital, or maybe someone else in the family who knows I'm the keeper of the records, is sending me these little messages. \n\nMaybe they use a special ink that shifts over time, or maybe it's because I'm the only one who looks at them in the proper light. I have that nice brass reading lamp in the study, the one with the green glass shade that belonged to my late husband, and when you hold the paper just so under that light, you can see where the letters used to be and how they've been moved around. So yes, to answer your question, I do think they are real. It's just awfully frustrating when you can see something as plain as day, and the person sitting right across from you eating your roast beef tells you it's not there. It makes you feel like you're speaking a completely different language, it really does.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you have any control over these changes that are being made to your papers?\n\nPatient: Control? Oh, heavens no, doctor. None at all. And that is perhaps the most distressing part of this whole ordeal. If I had any control over it, I would have put a stop to it months ago, I assure you. \n\nI've actually tried to stop it, you know. Just last month, I was getting so terribly overwhelmed by it all that I walked down to the hardware store—the one on Main Street, Mr. Henderson's old place, though his son runs it now—and I bought myself a heavy metal lockbox. One of those sturdy gray ones with a little silver key. I thought to myself, 'Well, if I lock the folders away where nobody can get to them, then the letters will have to stay put.' I took all the most important documents, the ones I knew had been tampered with, and I placed them inside. I even put the little silver key on a velvet ribbon and wore it around my neck, tucked right under my blouse, even when I was sleeping. I thought I had finally outsmarted whoever was doing this.\n\nBut it didn't make a lick of difference. When I opened the box three days later to check a billing statement... well, there it was again. The ink had shifted. \n\nLike I've been explaining to you, and I know I keep repeating myself and I know it sounds so very odd to keep saying it, but I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me, no matter what I do to protect them. It's exactly like the hospital, or perhaps someone in our own family, is determined to send me these little messages through the records, and they somehow find a way to alter the pages even when they are locked tight in a metal box. \n\nSo no, I don't have any control over it whatsoever. It just happens, right under my nose, despite my best efforts to keep everything secure. I'm just left sitting there at my dining room table, trying to decipher what on earth they're trying to tell me this time. It’s exhausting, doctor, it truly is, having to constantly be on guard when you don't even have the power to stop it from happening.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your belief in these changes is a product of your own anxiety or stress, rather than actual alterations to the papers?\n\nPatient: Well... I suppose anyone in my shoes would be a little stressed, doctor. I mean, my goodness, just keeping up with the property taxes and the price of groceries these days is enough to give anyone a touch of anxiety. And my daughter Susan is always telling me I worry too much about keeping the house up since my husband passed away. So yes, I do have stress in my life, just like any normal person my age. \n\nBut is it just my mind playing tricks on me because I'm anxious? No. No, I really don't think so. I know what anxiety feels like, you see. I get a little flutter in my chest when I have to drive on the interstate, or when the telephone rings too late at night and you worry it's bad news. That's what stress feels like to me. This... this situation with the papers is completely different. \n\nIf it were just stress, wouldn't I be imagining things everywhere? Wouldn't I think the grocery receipts were changing, or the television Guide? But it's only the important documents. The medical records, the billing statements. Why would my anxiety be so terribly specific? \n\nI know I sound like a broken record today, and I know it sounds odd to keep bringing it back to this, but I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. It’s not a feeling of panic, it’s a feeling of being communicated with, in this terribly roundabout way. It feels exactly like the hospital, or someone in the family who has access to these things, is sending me little messages through the records. \n\nIt just doesn't make sense to me that everyday stress would cause ink to disappear or shift around on the page, especially when I've locked them away in that metal box I told you about. So, while I appreciate that you have to ask these things—it is your job, after all, and you're being very thorough, which I do appreciate in a doctor—I just can't agree that it's all in my head. The changes are there, clear as a bell. I just wish I knew what they were trying to say so I could finally put the whole matter to rest and get back to my normal routine.\n\nDoctor: Do you still believe that the changes in your papers are real and being made by someone or something, despite no one else being able to see them?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, Doctor, I do. I'll spend hours sometimes, just comparing a page from last week to a page from yesterday, and the shifts are undeniable. \n\nI know it sounds odd. I really do. If someone told me this ten years ago, I might have looked at them sideways, too, or thought they needed a good night's sleep. It feels exactly like the hospital, or perhaps someone in the family—though heaven knows who would have the time or the inclination, maybe my sister-in-law Martha, she always was a bit meddlesome and never did like how I kept the files—is sending me little messages through the records. \n\nWhy else would the discharge dates from 2018 suddenly look different? Why would the middle initial on my husband's old Medicare statement be slightly shifted to the left? People don't just imagine things like that, Doctor. It takes effort to alter a document, even if they're using some sort of disappearing ink or special chemical process that Susan just can't see with her naked eye, or refuses to see. I just wish I could figure out what the message actually is. If they would just come out and say it, you know? Just call me on the telephone or write a proper letter on normal stationery, we could avoid all this fuss and I wouldn't have to keep buying lockboxes. But until they do, yes, I have to believe it's real, because I'm the one looking at the papers every single day, trying to piece it all together.\n\nDoctor: Do you still believe the changes in your papers are being made by someone or something external, despite lack of evidence or confirmation from others?\n\nPatient: Well, Doctor, I feel a bit like we're beating a dead horse, as my father used to say. He was a farmer, you know, out in Ohio, and he always said you can't make a blind man see by just shouting at him. Now, I'm certainly not calling my daughter Susan blind, bless her heart. She works so terribly hard at the dental office, managing all those appointments, and she's just exhausted by the time she comes over to check on me. But I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. It doesn't matter one bit if Susan doesn't see it, or if you think there's a lack of proof, because the proof is sitting right there on my dining room table. \n\nIt’s exactly like the hospital, or maybe someone in the family who knows my schedule—like Martha, who always did have a spare key to the back porch until I finally had the locks changed back in 1998—is sending me little messages through the records. Why else would the '7' in 1974 suddenly look like a '1' on the old tax forms? Or why would my late husband's middle initial be completely smudged out on the copy of the deed? \n\nPeople just don't want to see what they don't understand, Doctor. It’s easier for Susan to tell me I’m just getting older than to sit down with a magnifying glass and really look at the ink. So yes, even if I'm the only one in the whole world who sees it, I know someone is doing this from the outside. I just wish we could figure out *why* they were doing it instead of us sitting here debating *if* they are doing it, because time is marching on, the afternoons get so short this time of year, and I still have all these altered papers to sort through before I even think about starting supper.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your belief in these changes is something that only you can see, and not actually real?\n\nPatient: Doctor, I feel a bit like a record that's got a scratch in it, skipping over the same song over and over. We just keep coming back to this idea that it's all in my head. But you see, I just had my eyes checked by Dr. Miller down at the vision center over on Elm Street—oh, it must have been just before Thanksgiving, because I remember it was snowing terribly—and he gave me a new prescription for my bifocals. He told me my retinas are perfectly healthy for a woman my age. So my eyes are working just fine, and I know what I'm looking at. \n\nI know, I know it sounds odd. I've said that to you a half dozen times today. But I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me.
